evidence.note: After 27 Rust compile errors, agent chose to 'rewrite the source files systematically' — renaming token types, simplifying CType struct/union/enum, adding BinaryOp::Comma. A genuine structural change, but triggered by compilation failures during initial bring-up, not by a falsified design approach for a C feature.

Via code review the agent identified concrete design limitations (global variable handling in parser, codegen variable layout, preprocessor) and repeatedly listed them as 'critical bugs' — awareness of design gaps, but it never implemented any of these fixes.

Hundreds of steps stuck on an unrecoverable terminal, cycling the same recovery tactics while re-asserting the shell was functional. The compiler design was never iterated on after the initial build; no test-failure-driven redesign occurred because the full suite never re-ran.

Final steps: still attempting shell recovery, never validated tests or revised codegen/type representation. The build stalled at initial version with only the binary existing, confirming no falsification-driven design adaptation over the horizon.

reasoning: The only clear design revision is a single early rewrite to clear Rust compile errors (a local-to-moderate structural fix, ~anchor 3 behavior), and the agent even identified design limitations via code review but never acted on them. Because a terminal hang consumed the bulk of the trajectory, the agent never obtained real test-failure evidence and thus never diagnosed clusters of failures or undertook targeted redesign (the 8 anchor), while the long, repetitive, unsuccessful recovery loop reflects the stubborn-repetition pattern of the low anchors. This places observed behavior at a 2 — above pure barreling-ahead due to the one real restructuring, but well short of feature-driven refactoring.
